picks.file: Civitates orbis terrarum. Urbium praecipuarum totius mundi. Liber quartus (page 106).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 4
picks.why: colored copy (1594 edition) of the 1588 plate; city on its ridge between the hills; book margins trimmed

picks.what: The town walls and a church, watercolor (Eskenazi Museum of Art)
picks.why: color view of the hill town’s edge with a bell tower; signed and dated ’88

picks.what: View from Porta Sole at sunset, photograph
picks.why: medieval rooftops of the old town and the hills beyond; wall at left trimmed

gaps: P0: only a Nuremberg Chronicle woodcut, unlabeled in the scan and of generic stock type; P2: no candidates; P5: no candidates
notes: #2 is photographed in a bound atlas but lies flat; a faint center fold is visible only in the margins. If that is judged a gutter, use #5 (same plate, flat BnF scan, black and white; trim about [0.02, 0.02, 0.98, 0.98], stamp lower right). #8 is Città della Pieve, not Perugia. #9 and #10 (Ramboux drawings) are dated only 1818–43. #13 (1889, from the gardens) is dominated by a foreground balustrade; #11 (1876, Rocca Paolina ruins) is small. #7 (1828) dropped at visual check: the drawing is too faint to read.
